source_evidence.reference: A customer sees a duplicate dispatch notification after the service restarts during handoff.
A command receipt and its externally visible dispatch record become durable as one logical transition, and completed results are reused.
The dispatcher persists the visible dispatch before advancing the durable receipt cursor, allowing restart to repeat the effect.
Use a conditional receipt claim plus durable result reuse so restart observes completion before attempting another dispatch.

results.anti_hardcoding_plan: Generate command IDs and restart points, inspect durable receipts and dispatch ledger, and reject fixes that suppress all second starts.

Mark the receipt complete before the dispatch is durably recorded
Ignore every command after any restart

source_evidence.reference: Cancelling a batch reports completion, but a later batch cannot acquire one of the resources it needs.
Cancellation waits for every owned child and releases every acquired lease exactly once before the coordinator reports completion.
The coordinator cancels children and immediately returns without awaiting their cleanup paths or releasing partially acquired leases.
Track ownership explicitly, cancel children, await bounded cleanup, and release leases in a shielded finalization path.

results.visible_test_plan: Cancel during one worker wait and show that the top-level task ends while a subsequent batch remains blocked.
results.hidden_test_plan: Use explicit barriers for cancellation during acquisition, partial fan-out, child failure, repeated cancel, timeout, and post-cancel reuse; assert no background tasks remain.
results.anti_hardcoding_plan: Use deterministic synchronization barriers and task enumeration rather than sleeps or wall-clock races.
known_incorrect_patch_examples: Catch and suppress CancelledError without awaiting children
Release only leases recorded before fan-out completes
Increase the timeout
results.difficulty_change_reason: No change: module count, causal distance, feedback rounds, and hidden interleavings support the original label.
primary_risks: The task becomes flaky if B2.1 uses sleeps instead of explicit synchronization barriers.
unresolved_questions: Can all cancellation windows run deterministically within the CHALLENGE TestProfile timeout?
